hypothesis:
Second point on the attention-score softcap axis opened by the previous trial, at 15 instead of 30. The fa3 kernels apply sc*tanh(scores/sc) to attention logits internally at zero step cost; the model has never used this, though it softcaps its OUTPUT logits at 13.

Two points are the minimum that can distinguish the three outcomes that matter. If the loose cap at 30 helped, a tighter cap tells me whether the axis keeps paying or has already peaked. If the loose cap was null, that most likely means attention scores rarely reach 30, and the honest follow-up is to cap where the scores actually live rather than to conclude the mechanism is inert -- reading a loose-cap null as a dead axis is exactly the extrapolation-from-too-few-points error this campaign has made three times. If the loose cap hurt, 15 should hurt more, and the monotone confirmation is worth having before the mechanism is written off.

15 is chosen to sit just above the output softcap of 13, which is the one empirically tuned scale in this model and the best available prior for the magnitude at which capping a logit-like quantity starts to bite here.
change_summary: The same one-kwarg change as the previous trial at a different value: softcap=15.0 at both fa3 call sites. No new tensors, no new parameters, nothing crossing a kernel boundary. Same edit script and same guards -- exactly two un-softcapped sites required, refuses if a cap is already present, rejects 0.0 as fa3's disabled sentinel. Step count should not move.
expected_val_bpb_effect: Conditional on the previous arm, and I am registering the mapping now so it cannot be chosen after the fact. If 30 won, I expect 15 to win by more or to overshoot slightly, in the range -0.003 to +0.001. If 30 was null, I expect 15 to be where the mechanism first shows itself, somewhere in -0.002 to +0.002. If 30 lost, I expect 15 to lose more, and two monotone points close the axis honestly. Zero throughput cost, so the raw delta is the mechanism against the ~0.0012 n=1 floor; step count read first.
risk: A tighter cap is the more dangerous one. At 15 the cap is close enough to the working range of attention logits that it may act as a genuine nonlinearity rather than a tail bend, and the gradient of tanh saturates, which can slow early training in a way that shows up as a step-count-neutral but loss-worse run. That is a real outcome, not a failure, and I will report it as the mechanism rather than as instability unless the loss trace actually spikes. The interpretive risk is treating two points on a new axis as a shape: they establish direction and rough magnitude, not an optimum, and locating one would need a third.
